classification.difficultyReason: Translate six contexts into overlapping sets, identify the union or intersection and calculate intersection or outside-region counts.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A pair of dice was rolled 100 times. The sum of the numbers on the upturned faces was greater than 6 in 70 rolls, and less than 8 in 65 rolls. Draw a Venn diagram and find how many times this sum was 7.

answer.short:
35 times.

A sum of 7 belongs to both sets.
answer.worked:
Let $A$ be the rolls with a sum greater than 6 and $B$ the rolls with a sum less than 8. Every roll belongs to at least one set, and their intersection consists of the rolls with a sum of 7.

$$\begin{align*}|A\cap B|&=70+65-100\\|A\cap B|&=35\end{align*}$$

The sum was 7 on 35 rolls. The diagram has 35 in $A$ only, 35 in both sets, 30 in $B$ only and 0 outside.

spec.description: Authored count diagram for the requested student construction; A means sum greater than 6 and B means sum less than 8.
spec.mathematics: A only 35; intersection 35; B only 30; outside 0; universal total 100.

children.label: b
children.prompt: One hundred boys all play cricket or soccer. Eighty play cricket and 67 play soccer. Draw a Venn diagram and find out how many play both sports.

answer.worked:
Let $C$ represent cricket and $S$ soccer. All 100 boys belong to $C\cup S$.

$$\begin{align*}|C\cap S|&=80+67-100\\|C\cap S|&=47\end{align*}$$

47 boys play both sports. The remaining regions contain $80-47=33$ cricket-only players, $67-47=20$ soccer-only players and 0 outside.

spec.description: Authored count diagram; C represents cricket and S soccer.
spec.mathematics: Cricket only 33; both 47; soccer only 20; neither 0; total 100.

children.label: c
children.prompt: One hundred girls each wrote down the value of the coins in their pockets. Sixty of them had more than $\$1$ and 48 of them had less than $\$1.20$. Draw a Venn diagram to find how many of them had $\$1.05$, $\$1.10$ or $\$1.15$.

answer.short:
8 girls.

These amounts lie in the intersection of the two sets.
answer.worked:
Let $A$ represent amounts greater than $\$1$ and $B$ amounts less than $\$1.20$. Every amount belongs to at least one set. Amounts strictly between $\$1$ and $\$1.20$ are $\$1.05$, $\$1.10$ and $\$1.15$, using the source's 5-cent coin increments.

$$\begin{align*}|A\cap B|&=60+48-100\\|A\cap B|&=8\end{align*}$$

8 girls had one of the stated amounts. The diagram has 52 in $A$ only, 8 in both, 40 in $B$ only and 0 outside.

spec.description: Authored count diagram; A represents amounts greater than one dollar and B amounts less than one dollar twenty.
spec.mathematics: A only 52; intersection 8; B only 40; outside 0; total 100.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Among 100 concert-goers, 75 are singers, 65 are instrumentalists and 50 are both singers and instrumentalists. Draw a Venn diagram to find out how many are neither singers nor instrumentalists.

answer.worked:
Let $S$ represent singers and $I$ instrumentalists. The singer-only region contains $75-50=25$ and the instrumentalist-only region contains $65-50=15$.

$$\begin{align*}|S\cup I|&=75+65-50\\|S\cup I|&=90\\|(S\cup I)^c|&=100-90\\|(S\cup I)^c|&=10\end{align*}$$

10 concert-goers are neither singers nor instrumentalists.

spec.description: Authored count diagram retaining the outside region; S represents singers and I instrumentalists.
spec.mathematics: Singers only 25; both 50; instrumentalists only 15; neither 10; total 100.

children.label: e
children.prompt: A coin collector buys a bag containing 100 coins. Sixty-five are silver, 90 are round, and 61 are silver and round. Draw a Venn diagram to find out how many are neither silver nor round.

answer.worked:
Let $S$ represent silver coins and $R$ round coins. The silver-only region contains $65-61=4$ and the round-only region contains $90-61=29$.

$$\begin{align*}|S\cup R|&=65+90-61\\|S\cup R|&=94\\|(S\cup R)^c|&=100-94\\|(S\cup R)^c|&=6\end{align*}$$

6 coins are neither silver nor round.

spec.description: Authored count diagram retaining the outside region; S represents silver coins and R round coins.
spec.mathematics: Silver only 4; both 61; round only 29; neither 6; total 100.

children.label: f
children.prompt: One hundred and sixty students all play the piano or the violin. One hundred and twenty play the piano and 80 play the violin. How many play both?

answer.worked:
Let $P$ represent piano players and $V$ violin players. All 160 students belong to $P\cup V$.

$$\begin{align*}|P\cap V|&=120+80-160\\|P\cap V|&=40\end{align*}$$

40 students play both instruments.
